solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Astronomical list obviously includes this

indicators.note: includes says the letters sit inside the run of words just before it, spanning their joins

explanation.surface: A catalogue of heavenly bodies is bound to feature the thing in question.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the letters run from the end of 'Astronomical' through 'list' into 'obviously', and a moon of Jupiter would indeed appear on any astronomical list.
explanation.definitionFit: Callisto is one of the large Galilean moons of Jupiter, so it belongs on any list of heavenly bodies.

clue.text: Convincing chap to be prop for county

indicators.note: to be prop for says the chap sits underneath, holding up the county in this down entry

parts.note: a gent is a chap, a man

explanation.surface: A man persuades people he can support his county.
explanation.definitionFit: A cogent argument is forceful and persuasive.

clue.text: Note crumbs scattered over drink

parts.note: la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: scattered asks for the letters of crumbs to be strewn into a new order

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Crumbs scattered across a drink spilled after a musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' turns CRUMBS into MBRUSC; in cricket an over is a set of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambrusco is a sparkling red Italian wine, a drink.

clue.text: Spotted first priest leaving hint

indicators.note: leaving says the priest's letter departs from the word for spotted

parts.note: spotted skin is pimply

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word priest

explanation.surface: Seeing the priest go first is a clue to what is going on.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint is to suggest something without stating it, which is to imply it.

clue.text: Pipe that splits in two inside of chest

definitions.text: Pipe that splits in two inside of chest

parts.words: Pipe that splits in two inside of chest
parts.note: the windpipe runs down into the chest and divides into the two bronchi

explanation.walkthrough: There is no wordplay: the clue simply describes the windpipe, which forks into two bronchi, one for each lung.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the windpipe, the airway that branches into two bronchi within the chest.

clue.text: Red-faced seaman drunk

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword abbreviation for a sailor
a lush is a heavy drinker, a drunk

explanation.surface: A sailor who has had too much is flushed in the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablush is a literary adjective for blushing, with cheeks coloured by embarrassment.

clue.text: Damn close to sickness on rotten launches

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the next piece after the earlier ones

parts.note: blast! is a mild oath, like damn!

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of sickness

parts.note: food that has gone off is rotten

explanation.surface: Cursing at the end of an illness, on top of food gone bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket that blasts off is launched, so the phrasal verb matches launches.

clue.text: Release relatives when discovered

indicators.note: discovered is read as dis-covered, the covering outer letters stripped away

parts.note: aunties are relatives

explanation.surface: Family members are freed once they are found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when discovered' strips AUNTIES of its outer A and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie a knot or captive is to free or release it.

clue.text: Holiday flat he used with room below

indicators.note: below puts the room abbreviation under the rearranged letters in this down entry
used here means worked over, so the letters of flat he are rearranged

explanation.surface: For the break he used a flat with an extra room underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' rearranges FLAT HE into HALFTE. Half-term is a British school holiday of about a week in mid-term.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-term is a short school break in the middle of a British term, a holiday.

clue.text: Politician in local contest has new strategy

indicators.note: in places the politician within the local contest

parts.note: a gala is a local sporting event, such as a swimming gala
MEP, Member of the European Parliament

explanation.surface: An election candidate in a local race comes up with a fresh approach.
explanation.walkthrough: A gala is a local sports meeting in Britain, such as a swimming gala, which is why it can be a 'local contest'.
explanation.definitionFit: A game plan is a planned course of action, a synonym for strategy.

clue.text: Vehicle hired out for returning syndicate

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: returning says the word for hired out is read backwards

parts.note: to let property is to hire it out

explanation.surface: A rented car is being brought back on behalf of a business group.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartel is a group of firms acting together to fix prices, a kind of syndicate.

clue.text: Half of Mozart's first band

indicators.note: half of means only the second half of the composer's forename is kept

parts.note: Mozart's first name was Wolfgang

explanation.surface: Part of the opening group Mozart put together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mozart's first' is his first name, Wolfgang, not his first work.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang is a group of people acting together, a band.

clue.text: Nettlesome grass in front of yard

indicators.note: in front of puts the informer before the yard abbreviation

parts.note: grass and nark are both slang for a police informer

explanation.surface: Stinging weeds growing at the front of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' as an informer is British slang; the surface reads it as lawn, which is why nettles seem to fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Narky is British slang for irritable or snappish, and nettlesome likewise means easily irritated.

clue.text: Run in preliminary event and trounce Mo

indicators.note: in puts the run abbreviation inside the qualifying race

parts.note: a heat is a preliminary race leading to a final
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
to beat someone is to trounce them

explanation.surface: An athlete runs in a qualifying race and thrashes Mo Farah.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mo' suggests the runner Mo Farah, but it is British slang for a moment ('half a mo').
explanation.definitionFit: Mo is a short moment, and 'in a heartbeat' means in an instant, so both are a very brief time.

clue.text: Sat around hospital, mother makes a complaint

indicators.note: around tells us to move the letters of sat about into a new order

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother, having sat about in hospital, lodges a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' reads as a grievance, but here it means an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can be an ailment, and this chronic breathing disorder is one.

clue.text: Strong swimmer in fine condition

parts.note: hunky means strong and muscular
the dory is a fish, a swimmer

explanation.surface: A powerful swimmer in peak shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunky-dory is an informal adjective meaning fine or going well, so everything is in good order.

clue.text: Sailors steer clear of this noisy hound?

definitions.meaning: a small iceberg barely showing above the water, a hazard ships avoid
a dog that keeps snarling, the question mark marking a whimsical description

explanation.surface: Seafarers keep away from a dog that barks and snarls.
explanation.definitionFit: A growler is a small iceberg at sea, and also, whimsically, a dog that makes a low rumbling noise.

clue.text: Rock in shade beneath fruit trees

indicators.note: beneath places the shade word below the trees in this down entry

parts.note: limes are citrus trees bearing fruit
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A boulder sits in the shade below some fruit trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Limestone is a sedimentary rock made mostly of calcium carbonate.

clue.text: Key boozer lacking atmosphere perhaps

definitions.meaning: the long key on a keyboard that inserts a gap
a pub out in the void beyond the air, also one with no buzz

explanation.surface: The vital thing about a pub is that it has no atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: The space bar is the keyboard key for gaps, and whimsically a bar in airless outer space.

clue.text: Hope to organise veto for US city

indicators.note: to organise asks for the letters to be put into a fresh order

parts.note: to nix something is to veto it

explanation.surface: An aspiration to arrange a ban on behalf of an American town.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoenix is the state capital of Arizona, a large American city.

clue.text: Set up instrument to capture mass annual festival

indicators.note: set up in a down entry means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
to capture means the instrument holds the mass abbreviation inside it

parts.note: sax, the saxophone, is a musical instrument
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: Arrange a musical instrument to record a church service at a yearly celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: SAX takes in M to give SAMX, and 'Set up' turns that upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Xmas is the abbreviated name for Christmas, held every year on 25 December.

clue.text: Disgrace among footballers, well I never

parts.note: in can mean among, within a group
the FA is the Football Association, governing English football
my! is an exclamation of surprise, like well I never

explanation.surface: A scandal in the football world prompts a cry of astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The FA is the Football Association, which runs football in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamy is public notoriety and shame, close in sense to disgrace.

clue.text: Knew about filling poorly writer's vessel

indicators.note: filling puts the rearranged letters inside the word for poorly

parts.note: ill means poorly, unwell

indicators.note: about means the letters of knew are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone knew about a filling that had gone badly wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkwell is the pot holding ink for a pen, so a writer's container.

clue.text: Clubs don't keep model secret

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
to lose something is to fail to keep it
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so T can stand for model

explanation.surface: Golf clubs that never stay still are a hidden model.
explanation.definitionFit: Closet as an adjective means private or covert, as in a closet fan, so it means secret.

clue.text: Pass through vacant touristy island attraction

parts.note: to cut through is to pass through, as in cutting across a field

indicators.note: vacant means the inside of the word touristy is emptied, keeping its ends

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Travel past an empty tourist island's main sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacant' leaves only TY of 'touristy'. The Cutty Sark is a preserved tea clipper at Greenwich in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cutty Sark is a museum ship visited by tourists, so it is an attraction.

clue.text: Student left Alpine region

parts.note: a tyro is a beginner or learner

explanation.surface: A student has departed for the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb, departed, but it is the direction abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyrol is a mountainous region of the Alps in western Austria and northern Italy.

clue.text: Herb from the east of Brazil is abundant

indicators.note: from the east says the hidden letters are read backwards
of here means taken out of, so the letters are lifted from inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A herb grows abundantly in Brazil.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave no word for the hidden step; 'of' does that job. In an across clue 'from the east' means right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is an aromatic culinary plant, a common kitchen herb.

clue.text: Catch bishop suppressing papers

indicators.note: suppressing puts the bishop on top of the papers, pressing down on them in this down entry

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A bishop is caught hiding documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' is the noun: an angler's catch, here a freshwater fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Bream is a fish an angler might land, so it is an example of a catch.

clue.text: Temporarily acquire gold buried in hilltop

indicators.note: buried in puts the gold inside the hilltop word

parts.note: the brow of a hill is its top
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Gold has been buried at the top of a hill, waiting to be dug up for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: To borrow is to take something for a time, meaning to give it back.

clue.text: Liberal possibly sour succeeding old Vincent

indicators.note: succeeding places the rearranged letters after the singer's name

parts.note: Gene Vincent was a 1950s rock and roll singer

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of sour may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician may be in a sour mood after old Vincent's arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' with its capital suggests the political party, but it means generous; a capital at the start of a clue proves nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean lavish or open-handed, a synonym for giving freely.

clue.text: Switches places again

definitions.meaning: electrical devices that open or close a circuit when another current triggers them
sets down once more, as a carpet is laid a second time

explanation.surface: Someone changes seats again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Relays are electrically operated switches, and to re-lay something is to put it down again.

clue.text: Most engorged purply-red fly?

parts.note: plum is a dark purplish-red colour
a fly is an example of a pest, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A mosquito fat with blood, swollen and purplish.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumpest is the superlative of plump, fullest or roundest, so most swollen.
